statement.p: A closed rectangular box has volume 34\,\mbox{cm}^3. What are the lengths of the edges giving the minimum surface area?

p.em: (Give the three lengths as a comma separated list.)

static.solution:
x,y, z cm. Then the volume is given by V = xyz = 34.
The surface area S is given by S = 2xy+2xz+2yz. Substituting z = 34/(xy) gives S = 2xy +\frac{68}{y} + \frac{68}{x}. At a critical point, \frac{\partial S}{\partial x} = 2y - \frac{68}{x^2} = 0, and \frac{\partial S}{\partial y} = 2x - \frac{68}{y^2} = 0.
The symmetry of the equations (or by dividing the equations) tells us that x=y and so that 2x - \frac{68}{x^2} = 0, so that x^3 = 34, \quad\mbox{and so}\quad x = 34^{1/3}\mbox{ cm}. Thus the only critical point is x = y = (34)^{1/3} cm, and z = 34/\left ( (34)^{1/3} \cdot (34)^{1/3} \right ) = (34)^{1/3} cm. At the critical point S_{xx} S_{yy}-(S_{xy})^2= \frac{136}{x^3}\cdot\frac{136}{y^3}-2^2= \frac{(136)^2}{x^{3}y^{3}}-4. Since D>0 and S_{xx}>0 at this critical point, the critical point x = y = z = (34)^{1/3} is a local minimum. Since S\rightarrow\infty as x,y\rightarrow\infty, the local minimum is a global minimum.
